title: floor(x, options) skips an option equal to x
body:
`floor` in `boltons/mathutils.py` should return the largest option
that is less than or equal to x. When x is itself one of the options
it returns the next smaller one, or raises for the smallest:

```python
>>> floor(2.5, options=[1.5, 2.5, 4])
1.5    # expected 2.5
>>> floor(1.5, options=[1.5, 2.5, 4])
ValueError: no floor options less than or equal to: 1.5   # expected 1.5
```

Expected: an option equal to x is returned; a ValueError is raised
only when every option is greater than x.
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file

source.modifications: reformatted with black (layout and quote style only) to pass the repository formatting check; snapshot adds the injected defect, visible tests and empty package markers

defect: floor() uses bisect_left, which excludes an option equal to x.
